Steam Machine prices: from $480 all the way up to $5,000

I'm probably not in the right market for this sort of thing, but why is this so expensive? If I'm going to drop five grand on a machine that plays Steam games I'd rather build an amazing PC that has other functionality than just running games. Even on the low end, it seems expensive if they're trying to compete with Xbone and PS4.

The only thing separating these things from "real PCs" is the Steam OS, which AFAIK is simply a linux variant, so one would assume you could install Windows as well and dual boot. The most expensive on on the list (the $5k Falcon model) has the fastest i7 on the market, a Titan GPU, 8gb of RAM, and a couple SSDs wrapped up in a case that's only slightly larger than a PS4. I was just playing around on Falcon's site, and if you add every available upgrade to one of their Tiki models you're looking at over $7,600.

Even on the low end, it seems expensive if they're trying to compete with Xbone and PS4.

The $500 Alienware model on the low end has an i3, 2gb of GPU RAM, and 4gb of RAM, making it quite a bit more powerful than either of the consoles.

I thought it would be more limited but the Steam OS does seem to be a Debian variant, and they do have a dual boot Windows feature so that is nice.

My big concern is for people who don't have a Steam library and are just looking to play games on a console, is the power appeal of a Steam Machine enough to warrant buying one over one of the traditional consoles? $150 difference in Xbox One and the lower end machine can be pretty sizable.

I've been reading a lot of discussions about steam machines and I still don't understand who the target consumer is. I guess the manufacturers will have to sell a lot of units to make it worth their while. I just don't see that happening.

It seems to me that instead of this being a console competitor in the living room they have taken the worst of both worlds, pc and console gaming, and made this. It's way more expensive and not as convenient as a console on one side and has a worst performance/price ratio than a PC one the other.

$5K!!! The 1K or less models I can understand. They'd be good for folks who just have no clue about what parts to buy to have a decent gaming rig. But $5K is just insane. I was splurging when I put my battlestation together for 2K, but that included a bunch of peripherals like a monitor, gaming keyboard, gaming mouse, headset, and a webcam.

I downloaded MP2 on Steam and when trying to launch it the game didn't start. My Steam status changes to in-game and I could see a maxpayne.exe process in the task manager but nothing opened. I have win 7 64 bit. This is how I fixed the issue.

 

  1. Use the task manager to end the maxpayne.exe process (if there is one).

  2. Go to the game directory (e.g. “C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\Max Payne 2 The Fall of Max Payne).

  3. Create a new text document.

  4. In it copy this "start /affinity 1 MaxPayne2.exe".

  5. Save the file as a .bat file (image here).

  6. Start the game using this .bat file. You can create a desktop shortcut for it.
